title: Shared design system + customer-facing UI polish (BookingWidget, ManageBooking)
tech: React + TypeScript frontend only -- plain CSS (no new dependency, no Tailwind), consistent with this project's established minimal-new-dependencies convention
keyConstraints: Confirmed by reading the full frontend/src tree: there is currently no shared stylesheet, no design system, and no CSS framework anywhere in this project -- only two narrow, page-specific files (AdminCalendar.css, AdminServices.css) exist, and every other page (BookingWidget.tsx, ManageBooking.tsx, AdminDashboard.tsx, AdminAvailability.tsx, AdminLoginRequest.tsx, AdminLoginCallback.tsx) renders completely unstyled HTML elements with no className attributes at all. This task establishes the shared foundation and applies it to the two customer-facing pages only (BookingWidget.tsx, ManageBooking.tsx) -- admin pages are explicitly out of scope, to be handled as a separate follow-up task once this foundation is reviewed. Style direction: clean and minimal -- neutral, professional, understated (not a spa/wellness-themed look), works well against any future branding, and is the easiest tone to keep consistent as more pages get polished later. Add a new shared base stylesheet (e.g. frontend/src/styles/base.css, or similar -- exact file organization is Architect's call) defining CSS custom properties for a small color palette, a spacing scale, and typography, plus a handful of shared, reusable classes (buttons -- likely primary/secondary variants matching this app's existing primary-action vs. secondary-action button patterns, form fields/labels, error/alert text, loading text, card/container blocks) -- import it once globally (e.g. from main.tsx or an existing top-level entry point) so it's available to every page, not just these two. Critical non-negotiable constraint, confirmed by reading both test files directly: BookingWidget.test.tsx (9 query call sites) and ManageBooking.test.tsx (17 query call sites) both query exclusively via React Testing Library semantic queries -- getByText, getByRole, getByLabelText, getByTestId -- never by CSS class or snapshot. This means styling and adding className attributes is safe and should not break these tests, PROVIDED all existing visible text content, ARIA roles, label associations, and data-testid values are left completely unchanged -- do not rename, reword, or restructure any of that while restyling; only add classNames and CSS, don't touch text/roles/testids. Mobile-first is a real, established requirement in this project (not a suggestion) for every page built or touched since task 018 -- both these pages must be verified at a narrow (phone-width) viewport, not just designed desktop-first and adapted after.
description: Create a small, shared design system (CSS custom properties + a handful of reusable classes) applied globally, then use it to give BookingWidget.tsx (service select -> slot select -> booking form -> confirmation) and ManageBooking.tsx (view/cancel/reschedule via magic link) an actual visual design for the first time -- consistent spacing, typography hierarchy, styled buttons and form fields, clearly distinguished error/alert states, and a coherent look across both pages' several distinct steps/states. This is the first of two planned polish tasks -- admin-facing pages (List, Calendar, Availability, Services, Login) get their own follow-up task once this foundation exists and has been reviewed.
acceptanceCriteria: A new shared base stylesheet defines a small set of CSS custom properties (colors, spacing scale, typography) and is imported globally, available to every page in the app

A handful of reusable classes exist for the patterns that repeat across these two pages -- buttons (primary/secondary), form fields and labels, error/alert text, loading text, and a basic content-container/card pattern

BookingWidget.tsx's four steps (select-service, select-slot, form, confirmation) all use the shared design system consistently -- coherent spacing, typography, and button styling throughout, not just the first step
ManageBooking.tsx's states (loading, view, reschedule-in-progress, error) all use the shared design system consistently
All existing visible text, ARIA roles, label associations, and data-testid values are unchanged -- only className/CSS is added
The existing BookingWidget.test.tsx and ManageBooking.test.tsx suites continue to pass unmodified
Both pages verified usable and visually coherent at a narrow (phone-width) viewport, consistent with this project's established mobile-first requirement
No new dependency added -- plain CSS only
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in frontend/ (backend should be unaffected since no backend files change)
relevantFilePaths: frontend/test/BookingWidget.test.tsx (must keep passing unmodified -- reference for what queries must stay stable)
frontend/test/ManageBooking.test.tsx (must keep passing unmodified -- reference for what queries must stay stable)

frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.css and frontend/src/pages/AdminServices.css (existing CSS -- read-only reference for this project's current styling conventions, e.g. spacing units already in use, to stay consistent rather than invent new values arbitrarily)
securityConsiderations: None -- this is a purely visual/presentational change with no new data handling, no new API calls, and no change to any validation or business logic.
